---
title: Responsive navbar text
---

## Overview

A navbar item's `text:` can change with the width of the browser
window. Wide screens can show a full label, and narrower screens can
show a short one so that the item doesn't wrap onto a second line.

Give `text:` a map whose keys are breakpoint names instead of a single
string:

```yaml
website:
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: reference/index.qmd
        text:
          lg: API
          xxl: API Reference
```

This item shows "API" up to 1400px wide and "API Reference" at 1400px
and wider.

## Breakpoints

The keys are Bootstrap's breakpoint names:

| key | applies from |
|---|---|
| `xs` | 0 |
| `sm` | 576px |
| `md` | 768px |
| `lg` | 992px |
| `xl` | 1200px |
| `xxl` | 1400px |

Each variant applies from its breakpoint up to the next key in the
map. The lowest key also covers every narrower width, so the item
always has text and you don't need to write `xs`. In the example
above, "API" is also shown below 992px.

These are the same names that `collapse-below:` uses. If a theme
changes Bootstrap's `$grid-breakpoints` values, the text variants
follow the new widths.

## Full text in the collapsed menu

Below `collapse-below` (`lg` by default), the navbar collapses into a
menu that opens from a toggle button. In that menu, items are stacked
vertically and have room for their full labels. The text variants follow
the window width, not the navbar's state, so give the collapsed range
its own key:

```yaml
website:
  navbar:
    collapse-below: lg
    left:
      - href: docs/index.qmd
        text:
          xs: Documentation   # collapsed menu, below 992px
          lg: Docs            # expanded but narrow, 992px to 1200px
          xl: Documentation   # 1200px and wider
```

## Icon-only items

An empty string shows no text in its range. Combined with `icon:`,
this makes an item icon-only on narrower screens:

```yaml
website:
  navbar:
    right:
      - icon: github
        href: https://github.com/example/project
        text:
          xs: GitHub
          lg: ""
          xxl: GitHub
```

When some range shows no text, the link gets an `aria-label` with the
item's widest text, so screen readers can still name it. An
`aria-label:` that you write yourself takes precedence.

## Details

- Each variant is markdown, like an ordinary `text:` string.
- Variants work on `left` and `right` items, on dropdown menu
  toggles, and on items inside a dropdown `menu:`.
- Responsive text is a navbar feature. Sidebar and page-footer items
  with a map-valued `text:` show only the widest variant.
- A key that isn't a breakpoint name is ignored with a
  [`Q-13-18`](../../errors/navigation/Q-13-18.qmd) warning.
- Each variant renders as a `<span class="menu-text">` with
  Bootstrap's `d-*` display classes. These need a Bootstrap theme, so
  `theme: none` shows every variant.
